localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — roughly two weeks ago, not this week. That report (from Great Days Outdoors, featuring Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters) noted the first signs of the fall transition arriving in the bay: huge concentrations of baitfish — particularly greenies — pushing from deeper open water into bayous, flats, and bridge areas. Redfish sight-fishing on the flats was described as improving and expected to continue getting better through September into October as water temperatures begin to ease off their summer peak (water temp today at this location: 86°F). No specific trout, flounder, or black drum numbers were reported for the bay that week, but the arriving bait concentrations are a classic precursor to stronger inshore action across all those species.
